reason: Every entry is done or cannot-occur, and commitChecked names the commit that applied the goal-closing correctness pass rather than 2aab973 where the slice landed, since that pass ported hero_glyph's Upolyd disjunct and pinned three things the entries describe. The production game executes every done path: the fresh recipes in scripts/run-options-menu.mjs drive a debug-mode 'mO' menu to the wizmgender row and a configuration file that sets the option outright, and both discriminate against a port that draws the hero and a female pet plain. The development score is identical call for call, which is the guard this slice needed, since no development session picks the option. Three arms are done on a unit test alone and say so: the mimic and ridden arms, the male, female and neuter arms of the objnam.c suffix, whose CORPSTAT_RANDOM arm is the only one a level-generated object reaches, and statue_to_glyph()'s hallucinating gender draw, which is unobservable at its one caller.

boundary.startingEvent: A pick of the 'wizmgender' row from doset()'s full 'mO' menu in a debug-mode game, which options.c optfn_boolean() answers by setting go.opt_need_redraw and go.opt_need_glyph_reset. The same option is also settable from a configuration file, where optfn_boolean() returns at options.c:5325's go.opt_initial guard before reaching any of this.
boundary.endingEvent: The screen the port draws after reset_needed_visuals() returns, with every visible female monster and a female hero carrying the inverse video win/tty/wintty.c tty_print_glyph() gives MG_FEMALE under wizard && iflags.wizmgender.
boundary.validInputs: A debug-mode game, since wizmgender is set_wizonly and options.c:8842 hides its row outside one. Either gender of hero, since hero_glyph passes Ugender; a pet on the map, which exercises the MG_PET arm that sits above the MG_FEMALE disjunct; and iflags.hilite_pet either way, whose compiled-in default is Off.
boundary.observables: The attribute of every monster and hero cell after the repaint, and the screens and cursors of the debug-mode menu itself, which no recording has ever covered. No ported arm may consume randomness.
boundary.exclusions: Numbering the monster ranges in map memory, which no C writer does and this slice therefore does not. The invisible-monster range, whose writer display.c map_invisible() (378-385) is unported and whose arm raises MG_INVIS rather than a gender bit.

candidateListMethod.dispatchTablesAndCatalogs: display.h mon_to_glyph() (554-556), detected_mon_to_glyph() (557-559), ridden_mon_to_glyph() (560-562), pet_to_glyph() (563-565) and monnum_to_glyph() (639-641), each of which takes a gender code and picks a range from it. you.h:555 defines Ugender as ((Upolyd ? u.mfemale : flags.female) ? 1 : 0). objnam.c reads genders[].adj, which js/insight.js and js/player_selection.js already use.

The hero takes Ugender, which reads flags.female rather than any monster field.
candidateListMethod.javascriptCrossCheck: At the slice base, C's one ordered attribute chain is split across three sites in js/display.js: the third arm at print_glyph_attr(), the MG_PET arm at actualMonsterGlyphInfo() (glyph.attr = state.iflags.wc2_petattr ?? ATR_INVERSE), and MG_DETECT inline at presentedMonsterGlyphInfo(). grep -rn 'wizmgender' js/ returns only js/display.js's comment and test of the flag and two comment sites in js/options.js, so the objnam.c arm has neither a port nor a refusal.
candidateListMethod.remainingLimits: Two. The debug-mode 'mO' menu has never been recorded against C, so a first differential failure is as likely to be menu layout as the repaint: options.c:8820 sets endpass to set_wiznofuz under wizard, which adds ten boolean rows and two compound ones and widens longest_option_name(), moving the padding of every row and the page boundaries with it. And the recording depends on this environment's sysconf naming the user in WIZARDS; the checked-in template does not, so a fresh checkout cannot reproduce it.

entries.candidate: That map memory never holds a monster glyph number, which is what makes this slice a print-time change rather than a range conversion
entries.owner: None; it is the premise the slice rests on
entries.effects: Confirmed independently by the worker, which reached the same reading: 19 writers of levl[x][y].glyph, the nine in ball.c only copying a number another writer produced. The slice carries the bits on the live-drawn presentations, and monsterGenderFlag() reads mon->female directly, because C's own round trip is mon->female to a range to MG_MALE or MG_FEMALE.
entries.evidence: grep -rn 'levl\[.*\]\[.*\]\.glyph =' over nethack-c/upstream/src/ returns display.c:284, :302, :319, :359, :361, :436 and :555, all cmap, object, trap or engraving numbers; bones.c:569 writes GLYPH_UNEXPLORED; mkmaze.c:1840 writes a cmap number; ball.c's eleven sites restore a value saved from the same field. The one exception is display.c:382, map_invisible(), which writes the constant GLYPH_INVISIBLE, whose reset_glyphmap() arm raises MG_INVIS and no gender bit. detect.c:2205-2209 states the same rule in a comment.

sourceReview: Traced in two independent passes. The orchestrator traced the candidate list at 08c2151 before implementation, reading display.h hero_glyph and you.h Ugender, display.c's mgendercode assignment and its use in the M_AP_MONSTER arm, objnam.c:1549-1559, and every writer of levl[x][y].glyph across nethack-c/upstream/src/ -- which is what establishes that this slice is a print-time change rather than a range conversion, against a deferral that prescribed the conversion. The worker traced the same range while implementing, reached the same reading of the writers independently, and found two things the list did not hold: applyBooleanOption() had no wizmgender arm at all, and hallucinated_statue_glyph_info() made a gender draw it discarded. It also corrected the orchestrator's ' (neutral)' to role.c:690's 'neuter'. The trace covered state and random-number order: no ported arm consumes randomness except the statue draw, which already existed and whose result is now used rather than dropped. Stubs and stops identified: optfn_boolean() has one refusal left, on rest_on_space, which is outside this goal; the framecolor arm, the rogue-level terms and the worm-tail arms are unreachable for the conditions recorded above.
